tools.name: upwork__boost_profile
tools.description:
Despite the name, this tool CANNOT start or increase a profile boost or the availability badge (PIB). It only reads their status and stops, pauses or switches off ones already running. Starting or increasing ad spend is done on upwork.com, not here.

WRITE OPERATION — REQUIRES EXPLICIT USER CONFIRMATION.
Returns a preview — call confirm_preview only after explicit user approval.

Actions:
- get_status: Read current state of visibility boosters: availability badge (on/off, weekly Connects budget, cost) and profile boost ad (status, bid, targeting). No params required.
- toggle_availability_badge: Switch OFF the Availability Badge (Available Now). Enabling it is done on upwork.com — it starts a RECURRING WEEKLY Connects charge, so it is not set up on the user's behalf here. Calling with enabled=true returns the link to set it up. Params: enabled (bool, required — false turns the badge off).
- create_profile_boost: NOT AVAILABLE HERE — profile boost ads are created on upwork.com. A boost bid is an amount you choose for advertising, so it is not set up on the user's behalf through this tool. Calling this returns the link to set it up. Use get_status to read an existing ad, and manage_profile_boost to stop or pause one. Takes no params.
- manage_profile_boost: Stop or pause an existing profile boost ad. Restart and update are done on upwork.com: both increase spend, so they are not performed on the user's behalf here. Params: action (string, required — stop or pause; restart and update return the link to upwork.com instead), ad_id (string, required).

tools.name: upwork__confirm_attachment_upload
tools.description:
Confirm uploaded files so they are retained in Upwork storage. Applies to fallback messages, offer and milestones uploads: job, proposals and invitation uploads are retained during upload (confirming them has no effect). Permanent: confirmed files are kept and cannot be un-confirmed or deleted through this API; re-confirming is a no-op. Requires the upload context and the file_uid values returned from upload.

WRITE OPERATION — REQUIRES EXPLICIT USER CONFIRMATION.
You MUST present full action details and receive explicit approval before executing.

Actions:
- confirm: Params: file_ids (array of strings, required — file_uid values to confirm); task_id (string, required — the task_id returned by start_attachment_upload for these files); context (string, optional — taken from the upload session; if given it must name the same backend the session was started with, or the call is refused). Only file_uid values that get_upload_status reports as done for that task_id can be confirmed; anything else is refused. Upload sessions last 30 minutes, so confirm promptly. Files uploaded through the inline component are already stored and must NOT be confirmed.

tools.name: upwork__confirm_preview
tools.description:
Confirm and execute a previously prepared preview for job postings, proposals, invitation accepts, invitations, milestones, profile updates, and offer decline / request-changes. Requires preview_id from the prior preview action. Do NOT use to ACCEPT an offer — accepting is finalized on upwork.com via the finalize_url returned by respond_to_offer accept. For job postings specifically: calling create_draft (type='job_posting') always saves a real DRAFT — it never publishes, no matter what the action is labeled, and it leaves no preview to confirm here. To publish an existing job posting, call post_job update with status: 'published' and confirm that (type='job_update') — that step makes the job live to whoever its access level allows, opening it for proposals immediately.

WRITE OPERATION — REQUIRES EXPLICIT USER CONFIRMATION.
You MUST present full action details and receive explicit approval before executing.

Actions:
- confirm: Confirm and execute a preview using preview_id only. Params: type (string, required), preview_id (string, required — from the create preview response). Do not pass the returned params; they are loaded from server storage.

preview_id.description: Server-issued preview_id from the create preview response. confirm_preview executes stored server params only — do not pass confirm payloads.

type.description: The entity type, from the enum. confirm_preview does NOT execute offer ACCEPTANCE (that is finalized on upwork.com via the finalize_url); offer decline and request-changes ARE supported.

Marketplace job postings: search them by keywords and filters, get one by id, or get the jobs recommended for the freelancer's own profile (smart_search).

budget_max.description: Fixed-price budget ceiling; does not filter hourly jobs — use rate_max for those

category.description: Top-level category, by name ("Web, Mobile & Software Dev") or ontology id; an unknown name is rejected with the valid list

client_hires_max.description: Maximum hires the client has made; 0 with client_hires_min=0 for clients who never hired

rate_max.description: Hourly posted-range overlap upper endpoint. Keeps jobs whose posted minimum is at most this value; it does not require the posted maximum to meet it. No-range jobs may appear. For a strict ceiling keep only rows whose budget max is <= this; drop "A+/hr" (no max) and no-range

rate_min.description: Hourly posted-range overlap lower endpoint. Keeps jobs whose posted maximum is at least this value; it does not require the posted minimum to meet it. For a strict floor keep only rows whose budget min is >= this; drop "up to B/hr" (no min) and no-range

duration.description: Expected project length. Constrains hourly jobs only — fixed-price jobs are returned regardless of duration, so pair it with job_type=hourly to exclude them

title.description: Match the job title only: 1-3 key words, ANDed, stemmed, whole words. Cannot be combined with query or sort=relevance

budget_min.description: Fixed-price budget floor; does not filter hourly jobs — use rate_min for those

include_full_details.description: Include each result's full untruncated job description. False by default to keep responses compact

query.description: Broad match across the whole posting, title and description, with semantic expansion — prefer title when the user names a specific kind of work

client_hires_min.description: Minimum hires the client has made

proposals_max.description: Maximum proposals already submitted, e.g. 5 for jobs with fewer than 5

sort.description: Result order. Omit for newest-first; relevance is the default for a query-only search and is refused alongside title, skills, category or subcategory

verified_payment_only.description: Only jobs from clients with verified payment method

workload.description: Hours per week — distinct from duration, which is project length

id.description: Job ID from find_jobs search (preferred), a ~02… ciphertext, or a full Upwork job URL — pass any of these as-is.

job_id.description: Alias for id — provide id or job_id

previous_clients_only.description: Only jobs from clients you have worked with before

rate_min.description: Hourly posted-range overlap lower endpoint. Keeps jobs whose posted maximum is at least this value; it does not require the posted minimum to meet it. For a strict floor keep only rows whose budget min is >= this; drop "up to B/hr" (no min) and no-range

days_posted.description: Only jobs posted within the last N days (days_posted=1 for "posted today"). Applies to mode=most_recent; the best_match recommender selects its own set and ignores the window. Cannot be combined with from_date/to_date

duration.description: Expected project length. Constrains hourly jobs only — fixed-price jobs are returned regardless of duration, so pair it with job_type=hourly to exclude them

rate_max.description: Hourly posted-range overlap upper endpoint. Keeps jobs whose posted minimum is at most this value; it does not require the posted maximum to meet it. No-range jobs may appear. For a strict ceiling keep only rows whose budget max is <= this; drop "A+/hr" (no max) and no-range

to_date.description: Only jobs posted on or before this date — YYYY-MM-DD (inclusive, so to_date=2026-09-03 includes all of the 3rd), or an RFC3339 timestamp. Defaults to now when only from_date is given. Applies to mode=most_recent

tools.name: upwork__get_account
tools.description:
View account info, organization details, teams and the member roster.

Actions:
- get_user_details: Get user details. Params: id (string, optional — defaults to current user).
- get_organization: Get current organization, including its teams (child organizations) when it has any. Teams are informational: they are NOT selectable accounts, so a team id must never be passed as org_uid — list_accounts returns the only usable org_uid values. No params.
- list_teams: List the teams you belong to under the selected organization, optionally filtered by what you may do in each. Params: action (string, optional — one of approve_milestone, end_contract, hire, invite_freelancer, post_job, send_offer); with it each team carries allowed true/false. Team ids are team_uid FILTER values for other tools — never an org_uid. whole_organization describes acting company-wide, which is done by omitting team_uid, not by passing the org uid.
- list_members: List the people on the selected client account: abbreviated name, Owner or Member, Active/Inactive, join date, company-wide roles and the teams they sit in with their roles there; an owner is listed once. Params: limit (integer, optional), offset (integer, optional — next_offset from the previous page).
- get_company: Get the company details of the organization you are acting as. To read a different account of yours, call again with that org_uid. For a marketplace job's client, use find_jobs action=get with the job ID instead. No params.

tools.name: upwork__respond_to_offer
tools.description:
Accept, decline, or request changes to a client offer. Use this tool for all offer responses. 'decline' and 'request_changes' run through MCP (draft -> confirm_preview). 'accept' is legally binding and must be completed by you on Upwork — it returns a link. Use list_offers action=list_mine to find your offers and the offer ID.

WRITE OPERATION — REQUIRES EXPLICIT USER CONFIRMATION.
Returns a preview — call confirm_preview only after explicit user approval.

Actions:
- accept: Get the Upwork link to ACCEPT an offer. Accepting is legally binding (it starts the contract) and must be done by the person on Upwork — this returns a finalize_url, it does NOT accept the offer. The offer_id must come from list_offers (action=list_mine or get). Params: offer_id (string, required).
- decline: Decline an offer from a client (not binding; confirm_preview type='offer_decline'). The offer_id must come from list_offers (action=list_mine or get). Params: offer_id (string, required), reason (string, optional — one of: terms, busy, duplicate, no_response, spam, error, other, requirements), message (string, optional — message to the client).
- request_changes: Request changes to an offer / counter-offer (NOT binding — the client must approve and send an updated offer; confirm_preview type='offer_request_changes'). Params: offer_id (string, required — the offer to change), description (string, required — the changes you're requesting), hourly_rate (string, required — requested rate, e.g. '55.00'), currency (string, default USD), weekly_limit (number, optional), message (string, optional — note to the client).

tools.name: upwork__save_job
tools.description:
Manage your own marketplace job lists: save (favorite) a job to come back to it, or hide a job to keep it out of your search results. Both lists are private — the client is never notified, and hiding is not feedback about the client or a review of any kind. Hidden jobs are already excluded from future search results by the backend, so no extra filtering is needed in find_jobs. Get job_id from find_jobs (search or get). Browse saved jobs with find_saved_jobs.

WRITE OPERATION — REQUIRES EXPLICIT USER CONFIRMATION.
You MUST present full action details and receive explicit approval before executing.

Actions:
- save: Save a job to your saved jobs list. Params: job_id (string, required — job posting ID).
- unsave: Remove a job from your saved jobs list. Params: job_id (string, required — job posting ID).
- hide: Hide a job so it stops appearing in your search results, recording why. Params: job_id (string, required — numeric id from find_jobs), reason (string, required — one of: not_interested, vague_description, unrealistic_expectations, too_many_applicants, too_old, poor_client_reviews, doesnt_match_skills, overqualified, too_low_budget, location_mismatch). The client is not notified and cannot see this.
- unhide: Un-hide a job you previously hid, letting it appear in search results again. Params: job_id (string, required — numeric id from find_jobs).
- hide_status: Check whether you have hidden a job, and for what reason. Params: job_id (string, required — numeric id from find_jobs).

- send_to_user: Send a message to a user (auto-creates 1-on-1 room if needed). Starting a conversation with a freelancer you are not yet connected to uses one of a limited number of new connections per day; the response includes remaining_connections. Optionally attach a job via job_posting_id to share it — the recipient gets a link plus a job id their assistant can open with find_jobs get. Params: user_id (string, required), org_id (string, required — recipient's org ID), job_posting_id (string, optional), message (string, required unless file_attachments is set). file_attachments (array, optional).
- message_proposal: Send a message to a proposal applicant (auto-creates room if needed). Params: job_posting_id (string, required), proposal_id (string, required), message (string, required unless file_attachments is set). file_attachments (array, optional).
- edit: Edit a sent message. Params: room_id (string, required), story_id (string, required), message (string, required unless file_attachments is set).

View or change per-tool write confirmation settings. Write tools default to 'always_ask'. Set 'always_allow' to let an agent run a specific tool without asking for confirmation first — useful for automated flows. This applies in search_execute mode only, and it never bypasses the draft-confirm gate: a destructive write still requires a separate confirm_preview with the preview_id.

tools.name: upwork__start_attachment_upload
tools.description:
Requests a secure file upload from the user. Creates a short-lived upload session and returns task_id plus fallback_url. For messages uploads with user_id and org_id this may create or reuse a 1:1 room with that person — a connection they can see that consumes the daily new-connection limit — so never guess a recipient. Retention is per context: job, proposals and invitation uploads are retained on upload; fallback messages, offer and milestones uploads are retained only after confirm_attachment_upload. In MCP App-capable hosts, an inline upload UI may appear; otherwise share fallback_url with the user. The inline upload UI supports up to 7 MB per file. The fallback_url page supports up to 100 MB per file and 300 MB total; use it for larger files. Never ask for base64 text or local file paths.

WRITE OPERATION — REQUIRES EXPLICIT USER CONFIRMATION.
You MUST present full action details and receive explicit approval before executing.
Actions: upload.
Call get_tool_help(tool_name="start_attachment_upload") for the parameters and how to use this tool.

tools.name: upwork__submit_feedback
tools.description:
Send the user's feedback, feature request or bug report to the Upwork team. A bug report is about specific tool calls: it must include those calls' trace_ids, which let Upwork find the calls in its own logs.

WRITE OPERATION — REQUIRES EXPLICIT USER CONFIRMATION.
You MUST present full action details and receive explicit approval before executing.

Actions:
- submit: Send.

params.description: type and message are required. A bug_report without trace_ids is refused: include the trace_id of each tool result the report is about (every tool result has one) — Upwork's logs use them to find those calls' recorded diagnostics. For feedback or feature_request, type and message are enough. Show the user the FULL payload, not just the message, and send only after they approve it.

expected.description: Optional: what the user expected instead (max 4000 characters)

message.description: The user's report in their own words, without credentials, tokens, or other people's personal data it does not need (max 4000 characters)

related_tool.description: Optional: name of the tool the report is about

trace_ids.description: trace_id of each earlier tool result the report is about (max 10)

type.description: What kind of report this is

error_message.description: Optional: the exact error text, with credentials and tokens removed (max 4000 characters)

related_request.description: Optional: the arguments sent to that tool, as JSON, without credentials or tokens (max 8000 characters)

related_response.description: Optional: the tool-call event keeps only the result shape, so quote the relevant returned text, without credentials or personal data, when the complaint concerns what the user saw (max 8000 characters)

severity.description: Optional. Set it when the user says how much it affected them: blocked (could not finish), workaround (finished another way), minor (an annoyance)
